passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to The Coca-Cola Company's third quarter 2026 earnings results conference call. After today's prepared remarks, we will host a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press star one again. I will now hand the conference over to Todd Beiger, Vice President and Head of Investor Relations. Mr. Beiger, please go ahead.

passages.heading: Todd Beiger, Vice President and Head of Investor Relations
passages.text: Todd Beiger, Vice President and Head of Investor Relations: Good morning, and thank you for joining us. I am here with Henrique Braun, our Chief Executive Officer, and John Murphy, our President and Chief Financial Officer. We have posted schedules under financial information in the investor section of our company website. These reconcile certain non-GAAP financial measures that may be referred to this morning to results as reported under generally accepted accounting principles. You can also find schedules in the same section of our website that provide an analysis of our gross and operating margins. This call may contain forward-looking statements, including statements concerning long-term earnings objectives, which should be considered in conjunction with cautionary statements contained in our earnings release and the company's periodic SEC reports. Following prepared remarks, we will take your questions. Please limit yourself to one question. Re-enter the queue to ask follow-ups. Now, I will turn the call over to Henrique.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Thanks, Todd, and good morning, everyone. Our third quarter results reinforce the continued strength of The Coca-Cola system. We are acting with speed and discipline, enabling us to deliver strong results in an uneven environment. I want to start by thanking all our associates and bottling partners around the world. Every day, they serve customers, support communities, and bring our brands to life. This year has required resilience, agility, and strong execution, and our people have continued to rise to the occasion. Their efforts reinforce my confidence in our updated 2026 guidance and in the long-term opportunities ahead. This morning, I will provide an update on the global landscape and review our third quarter business performance. Then I will discuss how our system is delivering at scale and adapting locally to create durable growth. John will close with our financial results for the quarter, full year 2026 guidance, and some early considerations for 2027. First, the global operating environment continues to evolve. Geopolitical disruptions affect several parts of the world. Cost pressures have accelerated, and all of this has an impact on many consumers. Yet our confidence in the long-term opportunity remains unchanged. We have a strong portfolio of 32 billion-dollar brands and unmatched system reach with our bottling partners. These advantages matter, but so does what we do with them. For several years, we have been strengthening capabilities

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: around consumer recruitment, digital, revenue growth management, and system execution. By staying close to consumers and remaining constructively discontented, we continue to adapt in a dynamic environment. We are increasingly seeing that work reflected in our performance, including this quarter. Volume grew 5% and organic revenue grew 7%. Stepping back, our longer-term performance reflects a more balanced contribution to top-line growth. We expanded margins while continuing to invest in our business. We delivered double-digit comparable earnings per share growth and gained value share. Beyond the headline numbers, I am encouraged by how we are growing. Our disciplined investments in digital capabilities are creating momentum across many of our markets and brands. Yet, we know there is still more work to do. We continue to sharpen how we turn consumer insights into innovation, and we are balancing scale and intimacy to drive stronger execution across our system. Our focus is simple: keep learning and do a little better every day. This quarter, I spent much of my time with our people and bottling partners in several of our markets. These experiences always reinforce the importance of understanding local needs and responding to consumers, a strength of our system across the world. While every market is different, three themes were consistent. One, affordability is working. Two, both zero sugar and original taste are recruiting consumers. And three, execution and local

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: relevance are helping us win. Let me bring each of these to life across our business. Starting in North America, we grew revenue and gained value share for the quarter. Volume was even, due in part to the timing of the July 4th holiday and temporary challenges in certain finished goods businesses, but performance improved sequentially each month during the quarter. Across our total beverage portfolio, we had strong volume growth from many brands, including trademark Coca-Cola, fairlife, Powerade, Fresca, and smartwater. Mr. Pibb continued its success with another quarter of double-digit volume growth. We are applying our learnings from our strong sports playbook with the next iteration of Fan Work Is Thirsty Work, which brings Coca-Cola into football fandom through team packaging, retail activation, and locally relevant fan experiences. For Halloween, we are pairing Fanta's Haunted Universe with limited-edition Ghost Face Punch and collectible packaging that brings the experience from screen to shelf. We are also creating new opportunities across our portfolio. fairlife expanded its Nutrition Plan offerings with the return of fan-favorite vanilla, while BODYARMOR FIT brings sports hydration beyond the workout with a sparkling zero-sugar format with caffeine, electrolytes, and metabolism support. In Latin America, several key markets started the year facing difficult conditions, but our teams responded with market-specific actions that drove meaningful acceleration in the

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: third quarter. We grew volume, delivered balanced top-line growth, and gained value share with broad-based improvement across the region. In Mexico, the environment remains challenging, but we are seeing encouraging progress by combining affordability, strong revenue growth management capabilities, locally relevant marketing, and disciplined execution. In Brazil, momentum remained strong across our total beverage portfolio. Trademark Coca-Cola delivered another strong quarter, while Sprite and sports beverages also performed well. We continued to connect our brands with locally relevant passion points, including the Rock in Rio music festival, while also investing behind growth opportunities across our total beverage portfolio. In Argentina, the environment remains challenging. We have strong plans in place, and while there is still more work to do, we are encouraged by progress across the region. Moving to EMEA and starting with Europe. For the quarter, we grew volume, but we lost value share in a few key markets in Western Europe, and we are taking actions to improve performance. Following the FIFA World Cup, we transitioned into soccer activations around the English Premier League and Bundesliga while continuing to build everyday consumption occasions through our Meals platform. We are complementing these efforts with affordable propositions like our 500-milliliter Super Can and are continuing to focus on price pack architecture to help us recruit consumers and drive

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: transactions. In Africa, despite cycling a tough volume comparison, we gained value share and delivered high single-digit volume growth. We celebrated 75 years of The Coca-Cola system in Nigeria with an end-to-end activation. To meet evolving consumer needs in South Africa, we adapted an affordable single-serve package from India, giving it a locally relevant name, Mashesha, meaning quick. We also activated our Springboks rugby team partnership with the Be a Bok campaign and limited-edition collectible player cans. In Eurasia and the Middle East, ongoing geopolitical conflicts continue to disrupt business in parts of the region. Our system was resilient, delivering another strong quarter with volume growth and value share gains. From Coke Studio featuring Pakistani artists to affordability initiatives to locally relevant taste innovations like Sprite Cool Mint and Fanta Pomegranate, our teams are adapting to dynamic market conditions. Finally, in Asia Pacific, performance varied across our operating units, but we are encouraged by the progress in many markets. We gained value share and grew volume, revenue, and profit while price mix remained pressured due to a negative geographic mix and affordability initiatives. India delivered strong volume growth, with each of our top 10 brands growing double digits. We are expanding our consumer base by scaling both affordability and premiumization, strengthening execution, and leaning into emerging channels. For example, we expanded

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: our Sprite & Spicy platform into the QSR channel in India with meal combo activations, social media content, and influencer collaborations, which contributed to Sprite's volume growth of nearly 20% in the region. In China, the consumer environment remains subdued, with cautious spending and soft domestic demand. Despite this, we delivered another strong quarter of volume growth with strength in trademark Coca-Cola and Fanta. We continue to advance our digital capabilities to create more consumption occasions and connect with consumers in new ways. These actions are helping us drive immediate consumption packages and accelerate significant growth across digital commerce and emerging channels. In Japan, volume declined as consumers remained pressured in a challenging macroeconomic environment that was heavily impacted by adverse weather. For the quarter, we gained share, expanded our consumer base in trademark Coca-Cola, and accelerated Zero Sugar volume growth. We are adapting our offerings and executing to meet changing needs. In ASEAN and South Pacific, volume growth was broad-based across many key markets. Affordability, zero-sugar offerings, innovation, and stronger execution are helping us recruit consumers and create new growth opportunities, including the launch of Coca-Cola Zero Sugar in Thailand. In Vietnam, we are expanding our affordable single-serve package, which is now available in over 400,000 outlets with high repurchase rates. To sum it all up, while the

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: global operating environment remains uneven, we are encouraged by the momentum across our business and believe in our ability to deliver more for more markets and more for more brands. I am energized by the progress we are making across The Coca-Cola system. We are learning as we go, continuing to raise the bar, and finding new ways to create value. The actions we're taking are helping us deliver today while strengthening our ability to create value for the long term. With that, I'll turn the call over to John.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Thank you, Henrique, and good morning, everyone. Our results once again demonstrate the strength and adaptability of our business. For the quarter, organic revenue grew 7%. Our unit cases grew 5%. Our two-year, year-to-date volume growth average of 2% reflects a more sustained and balanced contribution to top-line revenue growth. Concentrate sales were two points ahead of unit case volume due to the timing of concentrate shipments. Price mix grew 1%. This was driven by four points of pricing actions, partially offset by three points of unfavorable mix, primarily due to geographic mix, timing of investments, and category mix. Comparable gross margin increased approximately 170 basis points, and comparable operating margin increased approximately 110 basis points. Both reflect underlying expansion, currency tailwinds, and a favorable structural impact from last year's sale of our finished product operations in Nigeria. Importantly, margin expansion did not come at the expense of investment, and we continue to drive greater productivity and efficiency across our operations. We are investing behind our brands and executing revenue growth management strategies that help us better serve consumers across brands, packages, price points, and occasions. Putting it all together, third quarter comparable earnings per share of $0.91 reflected an 11% increase, including a two-point benefit from currency tailwinds. Year-to-date free cash flow was $11.4

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: billion, an increase versus the prior year. Our balance sheet remains strong with our net debt leverage at 1.3 times EBITDA, which is below our target range of two to 2.5 times. We're continuing to judiciously manage our balance sheet as we await a court decision related to our ongoing dispute with the IRS. We are confident in our long-term free cash flow generation and the optionality it gives us as we move through the fourth quarter and into 2027. Our priorities remain the same: invest in our business and return capital to shareowners. Now, let me turn to guidance for full year 2026. We now expect organic revenue growth of at least 5%, which includes the impact of slight destocking and six fewer days in the fourth quarter. Our commodity exposure overall remains manageable. However, we are seeing elevated cost pressures in aggregate, driven by increased logistics and transportation costs. We now expect comparable currency-neutral earnings per share growth, excluding acquisitions and divestitures, of at least 9%. Divestitures are now expected to be an approximate 2% headwind to comparable net revenues, and we continue to expect an approximate 1% headwind to comparable earnings per share. This assumes the pending sale of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa closes during the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approvals. Based on current rates and our hedge positions, we continue to expect an approximate 1-point currency tailwind to comparable net revenues and continue to expect an

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: approximate three-point currency tailwind to comparable earnings per share for full year 2026. Our underlying effective tax rate for 2026 is now expected to be 19.7%. This reflects certain benefits in the current year that we do not expect to repeat going forward. All in, we now expect comparable earnings per share growth of at least 11% versus $3 in 2025. Finally, we now expect to generate at least $13 billion of free cash flow in 2026. There are some considerations to keep in mind for the rest of the year. As a reminder, the fourth quarter will have six fewer days versus the prior year. We also now expect slight destocking in the fourth quarter. Therefore, we expect concentrate shipments to slightly trail unit case volume for the full year. For the fourth quarter, following the anticipated refranchising of CCBA, we expect a four-point headwind to comparable net revenues, a three-point headwind to comparable earnings per share, and slight margin benefits. While it is too early to provide specific guidance for 2027, we do want to share some considerations based on what we know today. Overall, we expect consumer behavior to remain largely unchanged, with value being a very important consideration across all markets and income groups. The investments we've made to date and the actions we've taken across our business position us to enter 2027 ready to execute. With respect to commodities, we continue to manage various cost pressures and look for ways to navigate the

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: environment through productivity initiatives with our cross-enterprise procurement group and using all of our revenue growth management levers. At the same time, we'll continue to invest behind our brands, maintain disciplined cost management, and focus on expanding margins over time. With the anticipated refranchising of CCBA, we expect an eight-point headwind to comparable net revenues and a two-point headwind to comparable earnings per share, but expect positive impacts to both our margins and the return profile of our business. Additionally, as previously announced, we are exploring a potential IPO of our bottling operations in India and will provide further updates as appropriate. Regarding currency, if we assume current rates and our hedge positions, there would be a slight headwind to both comparable net revenues and comparable earnings per share for full year 2027. Many factors could impact both our currency outlook and broader business outlook between now and when we expect to provide guidance in February. To summarize, we are pleased with our third quarter performance. Our proven all-weather strategy continues to be our best ally to sustain our momentum for the rest of the year and into 2027. Across our many markets and operating environments, our people continue to rise to the occasion, and we are grateful for their dedication every day. With that, operator, we are ready to take questions.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone. To withdraw your question, press star one again. In the interest of time, we ask that you please limit yourself to one question. If you have any additional questions, you may rejoin the queue. Our first question comes from Dara Mohsenian from Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Dara Mohsenian, Analyst
passages.text: Dara Mohsenian, Analyst: Hey. Good morning. Obviously, another very strong unit case result in Q3 on top of Q2 strength, but the summer results were aided by events such as the FIFA World Cup and favorable weather. A, I wanted to touch on those events. It would be helpful to hear what you learned from the summer events with the FIFA World Cup and even America250, how you are using technology investments to enable the system to better activate those events, but also really how you are working to hold on to incremental customers or greater demand from existing customers during the events as you look across your brand portfolio. B, just maybe taking it broader, as you look out to 2027 across the business globally, can you discuss the challenge you see from cycling some of these tougher comparisons on the unit case side and how you think about the system's ability to continue to sustain volume growth going forward? Thanks.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Thank you, Dara. It is great to hear from you. Look, first of all, we are really excited with the results that we had in Q3 because it shows sustained and steady momentum that we had from the first half. It was important to continue that through Q3. If you are seeing the numbers that we are getting, it is more from more markets and more from more categories, and that showed up also in how we continue to gain value share globally. So it is 22 consecutive quarters of value share gain. We are feeling that we have the right momentum. The strategy is working in an environment that continues to be very dynamic. To your point about the FIFA World Cup, and specifically here in the U.S., also the America250 campaign, those were great moments for us to pressure-test our end-to-end activation, going from the brand strategy, the innovations that we brought to life, the revenue growth management, and execution coming in a very integrated way. We showed up really well as a system, not only in North America, but globally, and we leveraged that into Q3, and we're going to continue to leverage this in Q4 and 2027. Parts of the tech, data, and AI that we used during the FIFA World Cup, you're seeing in campaigns like Fanta Halloween, where you can see the connected packaging with great content and all the way down to a transaction. This brings us the ability to start pressure-testing the opportunities to drive more engagement all the way to transactions moving forward.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: The plans continue to be addressed market by market in an environment that continues to be very dynamic. We feel good about where we are right now for Q3 and building the plans for 2027 as well. To the point that you asked as well on what we're going to be bringing in for next year, I always start with the energy that we see with our bottlers and our customers when they see our plans year to date, and what we are laying up for the rest of the year and next year. Yes, we are cycling a year-to-date high-volume year, but we earned that. We got closer to the consumer and built flexibility into our plans to develop the right foundations to get where we are. We believe in our momentum, and we believe in the plans. A lot still has to happen until we get to next year, but we believe that we have everything under our control to guarantee that we continue to deliver on our long-term algorithm.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Carey from Wells Fargo Securities. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Chris Carey, Analyst
passages.text: Chris Carey, Analyst: Hi. Good morning, everyone. A key strategy coming into the year was to drive more balanced top line across volume and price mix. Certainly, as noted with Dara's question, you are on track for an exceptional year from a volume delivery standpoint, and you will have to compare against that going into next year, as you just noted. But one of the things that I wanted to drill into a bit was the price mix side, which, if it turns out to be about 2% this year, as we'll see, could prove one of the lower price mix years in about a decade. The question is really, as you go into 2027, how do you think the price mix strategy evolves so as to continue to deliver on the commitments that you have around your top-line algorithm? Within that, can you perhaps provide a bit of perspective on how much control you have over that price mix line? There is clearly a geographic mix, there is category mix, and you have pricing investments this year. I think underlying the question is just your ability to have control over the complexion of your top line, as opposed to there being headwinds coming at the price mix line that are perhaps out of your control as you go into next year. I would love any context on that. Thanks.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Thanks, Chris. A topic close to our hearts here. Let me just take a step back from the quarter—in fact, the last two quarters—and just remind you that when you think about the two-year volume CAGR, it is still around the 2% mark, maybe slightly above that, given the last two quarters. So we still feel good about the objective to deliver a balanced revenue algorithm: 2–3 points volume, 2–3 points price mix as we move forward. When you take into account some of the factors that have impacted our price mix numbers recently, it is worth unpacking a little bit. We mentioned in the script that we had four points of underlying pricing in the quarter, and that is pretty consistent with our year-to-date numbers. A little bit of higher inflation from a couple of markets in the emerging world, but pretty consistent. I think it is the mix piece that has had a bigger impact on that price mix number and maybe a little bit of a surprise to some. But within that, about two-thirds of it relates to actions that either we have taken ourselves proactively or reflects some of the inherent mix that has taken place this year, particularly with the finished goods performance. If you were to factor in the Topo Chico situation we have had this year, and you factor in the timing of investments, and take those out, our price mix for the year is pretty much within the band that we would look to deliver. As we go into 2027, it is a little early to give specifics on what we

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: expect for 2027, but just look at the volume CAGR and the volume momentum that we have been delivering. We are continuing to look closely across the world at pricing dynamics going into 2027. Inflation is one factor, but we also take into account a number of other factors: the state of the consumer market by market, the competitive environment, customer environment, et cetera. We will provide a little bit more color on that in February. On the mix piece, we will continue to see some geographic mix headwinds, just given the nature of the overall portfolio globally. The developing markets will continue, I believe, to outgrow some of the developed markets volumetrically. But two-thirds of the mix, as I said, this quarter were due to factors which we think are manageable going into next year.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Lauren Lieberman from Barclays. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Lauren Lieberman, Analyst
passages.text: Lauren Lieberman, Analyst: Great. Thanks. Good morning. Wanted to talk a little bit about reinvestment. I know the mantra is more with more, and it looks like this quarter, in terms of the reinvestment that went into SG&A, there was a lot of more. If you could just talk a bit about how much advertising and marketing was up, how much of this is sort of a set-the-stage into 2027. Because gross margins—and also, while we are on margins, underlying gross margin, I think in the slide, was up 70 basis points. Just curious how to think about that, right? You have talked about mix actually being a headwind. Is it just the absolute strength of the volumes flowing through that is driving that gross margin strength? So, marketing investments, where the SG&A dollars went, and then drivers of the underlying 70 basis points in gross margin. Thanks.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Yes, Lauren, thank you. Let me start with the gross margin numbers. As you are well aware, we think of gross margin in three distinctive buckets: the underlying strength of the business, structural, and currency. We are benefiting from some currency tailwinds this year. But the underlying numbers just reflect the quality of top line and the ongoing focus we have on managing our cost base. As you think about the underlying going forward, implied in our algorithm is modest expansion, and we believe we have the ability to sustain that as we go forward. Regarding the marketing investments, yes, we have taken a number of actions in recent months to set us up for a strong start to 2027. We have double-digit growth above the line, and we have a number of programs that we are working on in partnership with our bottlers to be ready for a strong start into 2027. I would expect, as we go forward, that we will have marketing investments growing more or less in line with gross margins to get the shape of the P&L where we want it to be, not just for 2027, but beyond.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Steve Powers from Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Steve Powers, Analyst
passages.text: Steve Powers, Analyst: Yes. Hey, great, thanks, and good morning. We have spoken about this before, but the reality is that a lot of the inflationary pressures facing the system today sit more heavily with your bottling partners than with the concentrate business itself. I guess in that context, as you approach collective 2027 planning, how would you characterize bottler economics today and their stance relative to those inflationary pressures? Any impacts that may be having on considerations around future pricing, investment levels, or just the way that system economics are shared as you think about the year ahead? Thank you.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Thank you, Steve. Look, first of all, we always look at that from a system point of view. Everything starts from how we are going to grow our plans, aligned with our brand plans per market. We feel that we have great plans for 2027, and we are actually anticipating that with investments this year, as we have done in previous years, to be ahead of the curve. That builds the momentum that we have and the flexibility during the year to continue to invest in those plans. Regarding costs, which are one input into the plan, the environment remains very fluid. Commodities have been manageable for us at this time. Looking forward, we are working with the bottlers right now through all the levers that we have as a system. One of them is our cross-enterprise procurement group, through which we procure the big commodities that we have for next year together. With that, we bring other levers into the equation, which are productivity, cost management, and our RGM tools, to ensure that we have an operational environment that can be totally linked with our growth plans for next year. More to come as we learn during the next few months. But so far, it has been something that we believe is going to be manageable in the overall scheme of things.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Filippo Falorni from Citi. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Filippo Falorni, Analyst
passages.text: Filippo Falorni, Analyst: Hi, good morning, everyone. I wanted to go back to the North America business. Henrique, you mentioned that there were a few impacts on volume being flat for the quarter, including the timing of the Fourth of July and some changes in the finished goods business. Can you expand a little bit more on that? Given that we see solid consumption data and tracked channels, are you expecting some improvement as we move forward? On price mix, I know you were cycling a difficult comp in Topo Chico and fairlife. How should we think about that, particularly that mix component, as we look ahead on price mix in North America? Thank you.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Filippo, thank you. On North America, let me step back and talk a little bit about the quarter and the year so far. We continue to see solid performance in North America. We grew this quarter. Revenue grew, we gained value share, we expanded margins, and we got pricing in line with inflation. That was really important. It shows that the brands have the equity and the right to take price. We kept investing in our brands. The impact that you're mentioning on the price mix was definitely affected by cycling a very strong prior year on some of the premium brands that were generated through our finished goods, including Topo Chico, as you know, and BODYARMOR as well. With that in the equation, if you take that out, and you take the impact of the July 4th holiday that fell into the second quarter, as we mentioned before, we would see volume growth. We see the momentum is still there. In terms of the strength of our strategy and our brands, we also feel confident that we have pretty good momentum, especially with trademark Coca-Cola, which grew again this quarter. Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Zero, especially Coca-Cola Zero, grew double digits again, and fairlife continues to do really well. POWERADE also grew, and we have other areas where we have work to do, which is always good for us and reinforces our motto of being constructively discontented. One of them is to improve performance on Sprite and BODYARMOR and our supply chain going into next year. All in all,

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: we believe that we have good momentum as a system and the right plans to navigate through the rest of the year and into 2027.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Yeah, I would just add, Filippo, if you are looking at the overall volume number, the restaurant industry continues to be under pressure. When you are looking at the scanner data, I think you are seeing a stronger business at home versus away from home, largely driven by consumer pressures that we have talked about in the past. While our own business continues to have a lot of momentum across those channels, I think the underlying pressure across the consumer landscape is there, and I think it will be there for the rest of the year as we go into 2027.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Yeah.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Andrea Teixeira from JPMorgan. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Andrea Teixeira, Analyst
passages.text: Andrea Teixeira, Analyst: Hi, good morning, everyone. I have a question exploring the theme of affordability and, of course, among all the CPGs, you have significant brand equity. How should we be thinking about list pricing? Your bottling partners have historically been able to take pricing in the low single digits. If we put the geographical mix aside, do you think you still can count on RGM capabilities that would allow some selective pricing while protecting the entry price points? A clarification on the fourth quarter. You obviously raised guidance, and you have the six fewer selling days. John, you called out the destocking comment, but you had also said that in the third quarter. It was ahead of the third quarter. I was hoping to think about how it is a wide range. Of course, a minimum of five allows you to have a wide range there. Just thinking about demand and destocking, how should we think about how many points of headwind that could be? Thank you.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Okay, Andrea, I will start with your question, especially on our strategy on affordability, and John can chime in on the outlook. Look, affordability needs to be looked at in the full context of revenue growth management. It is one of the legs of how we get closer to the consumer these days. Premiumization is equally important, so we always look at both. What we are seeing across the world—and this is something that I have seen especially on my travel in the last quarter, dividing and conquering here with John going to different parts of the world—is that value continues to be something that cuts across every market and every consumer that we see all over the world. And value means different things for the consumer, which then touches on affordability and premiumization in a way that we capitalize on in our plans. Let me elaborate on that. On affordability, what we always look at is whether we have the right value, the relevance of that brand, and an option worth choosing for the consumer to keep them in the franchise. If the answer is yes, we continue to push forward and get more coverage of that packaging format. If not, we adapt our plans and put that in place. A good example of that is what we did in Africa, building on what we have learned in India, where they had one package, a single-serve PET package with plasma technology that can allow you to go on longer routes and still keep the shelf life high. Now we imported that into Africa, and that

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: addresses affordability in both of these markets. It is going to continue to be very important moving forward because the consumer loves the brands, but needs to be closer to what they can afford. On the premiumization side, that is equally important in this equation. We play at the category mix. There are a few brands that continue to help us with that. In North America, you have Core Power and smartwater, and in other parts of the world there are also different packaging sizes that allow us to play with convenience. That value equation for the consumer also works really well. In the overall RGM strategy, we end up delivering what we need. So it goes in tandem: affordability and premiumization. That is what you are going to see not only for the rest of the year, but building into 2027. John, if you want to add on that.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Yeah, Andrea, the whole marriage of unit cases with our concentrate shipments this year has proven to be perhaps the more challenging year since I have been around, for a few reasons. You have the first quarter and the fourth quarter, with plus six and minus six days. As we have seen since the start of the year around the world, we have an external environment that is quite unpredictable, and I think our system has a tendency to want to get ahead of that. So the expectation that we highlighted in guidance reflects the best information we have at the moment. There are a couple of our segments where we do expect to see some destocking on the back of what has happened year to date. But we have still got some distance to go in the year, and we are keeping a close eye on this area. With six fewer days, it's difficult to predict cutoffs accurately as we move toward the end of the year. That's the best information we have at the moment, based on all the inputs we get from around the world. If there are changes through the quarter, we'll certainly have the opportunity to update closer to the end of the year.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Ottenstein from Evercore. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Robert Ottenstein, Analyst
passages.text: Robert Ottenstein, Analyst: Great. Thank you very much. You had a pretty nice increase in your guidance for free cash flow. Your leverage is down to, I think, 1.3, you said. I was wondering if you could talk about the drivers of free cash flow. Then you mentioned in the opening comments about increased optionality from your strong free cash flow and balance sheet going into 2027. Maybe if you could elaborate on that and then put these comments in the context of potential outcomes from the IRS case. Thank you.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Thank you. Let me take those one by one. Free cash flow year to date has three primary drivers. The first and most important one is that underlying business performance has been strong. We continue to make progress on working capital initiatives. Our cash conversion cycle, if I get it correct, is as good as it's been for many years at the moment. Then we have some timing that'll play its way through the rest of the year. For example, our CapEx year to date is a little behind what you would typically expect, and we expect that to make up in the fourth quarter. The key message, though, is that free cash flow is strong, and we've got momentum as we close out the year and go into next year. We've used the word optionality very deliberately over the last number of months because we are in a situation where we're anticipating a decision in the coming months in the IRS case. At the same time, we continue to think ahead as to the various outcomes that that decision could generate and feel good about where we are with respect to being able to manage a best- and worst-case scenario. The name of the game has really been to strengthen the balance sheet. I believe our balance sheet today is in as good a shape as it's been for many years, and to be ready in 2027 to deliver on the priorities that we outlined in the script. We'll continue to invest in the business, primarily in the short term, organically. We remain open to other opportunities. We don't see

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: them on the immediate horizon. As always, we're here to return capital to our shareowners. Again, at the moment, that's primarily through our dividend. So, think of the work to date as focused on strengthening the balance sheet, being ready for a decision and the outcome of that decision, doing the right thing for the business, and being ready for whatever that might mean in 2027 and 2028.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Peter Grom from UBS. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Peter Grom, Analyst
passages.text: Peter Grom, Analyst: Great. Thank you. Good morning, everyone. I wanted to follow up on Filippo's question on North America. You touched on some of the timing dynamics, but you also mentioned that you saw sequential improvement in volume performance each month throughout the quarter. So I was wondering if you could elaborate on that, and have you seen that momentum continue into the fourth quarter? Then, John, you touched on the at-home versus away-from-home component. I'd be curious if you've seen any notable shifts in that dynamic as the year has progressed. Thanks.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: On the volume, yes, we saw that improvement month on month during the quarter. The biggest impact was really what we said before: the July 4th impact that fell into Q2. We knew that we would start the first month of the quarter lagging behind it. What we have seen, and I mentioned this, when we look at the overall flat volume for the quarter, is that we are also cycling a good performance from Topo Chico last year, which has an impact on that. We just got back with Topo Chico in Texas, so it is great news, I think, to everybody and to the consumers that have been waiting for too long. It is the first step back, and we will sequence that moving into 2027. That volume will start to come back. Definitely, it is something that we are looking forward to. The other factor is really the momentum that we have. We grew trademark Coca-Cola, as we mentioned, with really good growth on the Zero variant as well. fairlife continues to grow. Powerade grew as well. Fresca and Mr. Pibb have been another very good surprise. They are still small in overall volume to impact the overall volume for North America, but within the innovation pipeline, it is something that we are very excited about. All in all, what we see is that we have the momentum and the right plans in place. But we are also going into Q4, which is important to reinforce: it is the biggest quarter that we had in North America last year, and we have six fewer days. You need to put that into the equation. But

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: when you look at daily average sales, we have the momentum that was built over the quarter.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Peter Galbo from Bank of America. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Peter Galbo, Analyst
passages.text: Peter Galbo, Analyst: Hey, good morning. Thanks for taking the question. John, I was just hoping to get maybe a clarification, and then the question is tied to that. On the currency FX guidance for 2027, I just wanted to understand if that was updated through yesterday and the context of it being that, obviously, there have been some pretty big currency movements even in the last 48 hours in some big, important markets for you. I know you caveated your commentary that there are many factors that could impact currency between now and February, but I just want to understand in real time how you are thinking about that, given some of the moves that we have had and whether that is embedded in the slight headwind outlook that you have for 2027 at this point. Thanks very much.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Yeah, great question. The short answer is no. We need to take into account what's unfolded over the last 24 to 48 hours. We will continue to do so. As you've seen throughout the year, there's been quite a lot of movement. So it's one we're watching very carefully. If there's sufficient movement over the course of the next number of weeks, we certainly would want to provide an update on that. As I say, there's been quite a lot of swings throughout the course of this year. It's one to keep watch on. But the numbers that I talked about in the script do not reflect the movement in the BRL, particularly over the last day or two.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Kaumil Gajrawala from Jefferies. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Kaumil Gajrawala, Analyst
passages.text: Kaumil Gajrawala, Analyst: Hey, guys. I guess first, sorry to belabor the point, but just for purposes of clarity, on the destocking, is the full year intended to be below, in line, or above in terms of concentrate versus shipments? Maybe if there are particular regions where the destocking is expected to occur, I think that'd be useful. On gross margin, with such a strong concentrate shipment number, can you give some context on leverage on the gross margin and maybe leverage on the SG&A line as well, and how it sort of works top to bottom? Because you probably won't have this spread going forward. To what degree can you help us forecast what margins would look like in the context of maybe better-aligned unit case volume and gross margins? Thank you.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: Sure. On the destocking, as I said in the previous question on this topic, it's somewhat of an anomalous year in trying to predict exactly. Right now, if you ask me, we expect shipments to run slightly behind volumes for the full year. That's our ingoing assumption that's linked to the guidance that we've provided. As I've said, there's a lot happening around the world, and there's every possibility that that could deviate. But that's the ingoing assumption as we head into the rest of the year. On your margin question, if I line up cases, shipments, everything else, we expect to have margin expansion for the full year. Again, the exact amounts that we're anticipating are really on trend with what we've seen thus far this year.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Grundy from BNP Paribas. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Kevin Grundy, Analyst
passages.text: Kevin Grundy, Analyst: Great. Thanks. Good morning, everyone, and congratulations on another strong quarter. You've mentioned the brand twice, but haven't spent a lot of time on the strategy, and that's fairlife, which has been a fantastic success story. Additional capacity came on this year, so we've seen a nice reacceleration in the scanner data. So, a few questions related to the brand. One, can you talk about updated plans and how you're defining success? Two, where do you see the brand sourcing occasions at the moment? And then three, maybe an update on the opportunity for the brand outside of the U.S., understanding the supply chain complexities. So thank you.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Okay. Thanks, Kevin. Look, we love the brand, as you know, and it has had fantastic performance. We're pleased to see, number one, another quarter of strong, double-digit growth across all the variants: fairlife, the Nutrition Plan, and also Core Power. That has been really encouraging. You remember that at the beginning of the year, we were still lagging behind demand and supply with the ramp-up of Webster. So we're getting better and better at that with the ramp-up of the plant, to the extent that we were able to launch a new flavor for Nutrition Plan, the vanilla flavor, which is doing really well as well. We already announced that we're going to have banana flavor in the pipeline going into 2027, which is great. We have a lot of fans for that flavor, and it's something that we always wanted to start expanding. So the good news is we're getting the product back on the shelf to keep up with demand, and the pipeline looks strong going into 2027. When you look at overall investment ahead of the United States and Canada that we have today, we're still working around it. The brand has tremendous equity value, and that is going to be embedded into our long-range plan. So, more to come on that. But the number one priority for us right now is to keep up with demand in these markets because there's still plenty of growth opportunities for us, and it's an important component of our growth moving forward.

passages.heading: Operator, Operator
passages.text: Operator, Operator: Our last question today comes from Bonnie Herzog from Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead. Your line is open.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: Bonnie? Maybe on mute.

passages.heading: John Murphy, President and CFO
passages.text: John Murphy, President and CFO: There is no Bonnie.

passages.heading: Henrique Braun, CEO
passages.text: Henrique Braun, CEO: I think we got to the end then. Okay, great. Look, to close us out, our performance reflects the hard work of our teams and partners around the world, who continue to stay close to consumers and do a little bit better every day, and we are very pleased with that. We are confident in our ability to deliver our 2026 and long-term objectives. Thank you for your interest, for your investment in our company, and for joining us this morning. Thank you so much.
